Author: Samit Gopal

Revisionist :- Munna Lal
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.

sentences.text: List revised.

2. Heard Sri Amit Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for the revisionist, Sri Devendra Nath Mishra,
learned counsel for the State of U.P. and perused the records.
3.

The present revision has been filed by the revisionist Munna Lal with the following prayers:-
"It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble court may graciously be pleased to call for the record of the case, allow the criminal revision, set aside the judgment and order dated 18.9.2008 of the court below and the appellant may be acquitted.
Munna Lal vs State Of U.P. on 29 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128540476/
1

entities.text: Munna Lal vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is, further prayed that during the pendency of the criminal revision before this Hon'ble court the revisionist may be release on bail and realization of fine imposed against them may kindly be stayed, otherwise the revisionist suffer irreparable loss and injury.
And/or
may pass such other and further order which this Hon'ble court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of case."
4. The trial court records were summoned which have been received and are tagged with the present revision which have also been perused.

5. The case of the prosecution as initiated on the basis of a complaint dated 24.01.2002 filed by the Food Inspector J.P. Tripathi for offences under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is that on 27.12.2002 at about 10:00 am while being on regular inspection he reached Bareilly Mod Crossing where he found the accused Munna Lal present in a shop which had Peda,
Barfi, Samosa, Tea etc. for human consumption to be sold.
The said food articles were kept in open and were thus found exposed to dust and flies were sitting on it.
He asked for a license of the shop which could not be shown by the accused.
The material was considered by him to be unfit for human consumption.
He gave his introduction to the people present there and asked them to be witness of the raid to which the people refused.

He then filed a complaint dated 24.01.2002 for offences punishable under Section 7(iii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rule 49, 50 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 against the revisionist.
6. The trial court framed charges against the revisionist vide order dated 06.04.2004 for offence under Section 7/16 of the Food Adulteration Act.
7. In the trial, the complainant J.P. Tripathi was examined as PW-1.

The accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C. took up the case that he has a PCO beside the said shop and filed its demand letter,
telephone bill and filed a license issued under the Food Adulteration Act in the name of Shyam Babu for the said shop which was raided.
Shyam Babu was produced as DW-1.

The trial court came to the conclusion that the case of the prosecution is beyond reasonable doubt and convicted the revisionist and sentenced him under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for six months R.I. along with fine of Rs. 1,000/- and in default of payment of fine two months simple imprisonment.
8.

An appeal was preferred against the said judgment and order of conviction being Crl. Appeal No.
30/2004 which was rejected vide judgment and order dated 18.09.2008 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 8, Shahjahanpur and the judgment and order of the trial court was affirmed.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 8, Shahjahanpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The present revision has thus been filed before this Court.
9. Learned counsel for the revisionist submitted that the revisionist has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is submitted that no sample of any food material was taken by the complainant/Food Inspector to substantiate the claim of the material being unfit for human consumption and adulterated.

It is submitted that there is no public witness of the incident which is Munna Lal vs State Of U.P. on 29 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128540476/
2 the admitted case of the prosecution case.

entities.text: Munna Lal vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further argued that in so far as the case of the revisionist that he is not the owner of the shop in question but is the owner of a PCO beside the said shop and further that license of the said shop is in the name of Shyam Babu for selling food items has not been found to be false by the trial court.

It is submitted that in so far as the license for selling food items is concerned, the same was not disputed to be not of the said shop and in the name of Shyam Babu the brother of the revisionist and a disputed document.

It is argued that no sample of the material alleged to be adulterated and found to be infested with dust on which flies were said to be sitting, was collected as sample by the Food Analyst/Complainant/PW-1 for sending it to analyst for reaching to a conclusion of the same to be unfit for human consumption.

It is submitted that the appellate court has without going into merits of the matter and without recording the arguments of the appeal and also without appreciating the evidence of a sole prosecution witness, the defence of the revisionist accused as stated under Section 313 Cr.P.C., the defence documents and defence witness Shyam Babu DW-1 dismissed the appeal in a very cryptic manner by just recording a finding that there is no irregularity or illegality in the judgment of the trial court and as such the appeal is rejected.
It is argued that there is no credible evidence to connect the revisionist in the present case.
It is argued that the revision be thus allowed.

10. Learned counsel for the Sate per contra opposed the revision vehemently and submitted that the trial court has given cogent and justifiable findings while convicting the revisionist after holding him guilty in the matter.
The case has been proved against the revisionist beyond all reasonable doubt and as such the judgment of the trial court is just and proper.

Although the judgment and order dated 18.09.2008 of the appellate court was also being tried to be justified by learned counsel for the State but efforts could not be successful inasmuch as there was no discussion of the merits of the matter, the evidence of the case and also the case of the accused appellant herein.
He submits that the revision be rejected.

11. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the complainant/PW-1 alleges to have conducted a raid at a shop selling food items wherein he states that the said articles being sweets and tea were kept in an open and thus were exposed to dust and even flies were sitting on it.
He came to a conclusion that the same are unfit for human consumption and thus adulterated.
There is no public witness to the same.
No sample of the food articles were drawn and taken by the Food Inspector for sending it to the Food Analyst for reaching a conclusion that the same are adulterated and unfit for human consumption.

The appellate court has in a very cryptic manner in five paragraphs without adverting the merits of the matter, the statement of the witness including the defence witness, the defence of the accused and the documents produced by him, dismissed the appeal.

Since the prosecution suffers from inherent shortcomings as no sample was drawn of the food items which was thus not sent for analysis to the expert, there is no public witness of the alleged incident, the case of the defence that the revisionist is having a shop of PCO adjacent to the shop in dispute and a license of the shop in dispute is in the name of Shyam Babu which are not disputed
, the prosecution against the revisionist cannot stand.
12. Looking to the facts of the case, the present revision is allowed.
The impugned judgment and order dated 18.9.2008 passed by Additional Session Judge, Court No.8, Shahjahanpur is hereby set aside.
